PullRequest.Title: chat: respect custom agent targets in Configure Tools
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #345908.

## Changes

- Resolve the agent target from its header, falling back to the active session's harness, including when the code lens is invoked.
- Enable the tools code lens for Copilot agents and reuse the target-aware completion catalogue, offering only effectively available tools.
- Group Copilot tools into a checkbox tree under **Built-In** and namespaces such as **vscode** and **browser**. Child labels omit the parent namespace; IDs, accessible labels, and saved references remain fully qualified.
- Preserve authored references outside the editable catalogue, cancellation, undo, and the existing VS Code agent/prompt-file picker.
- Add regression tests; move provider registration into the shared contribution so importing the provider in tests does not register a global editor feature.

## Validation

After rebasing onto current `origin/main`:

- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only` - passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/promptSyntax/promptToolsCodeLensProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/promptSyntax/promptFileRewriter.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/promptSyntax/languageProviders/promptHeaderAutocompletion.test.ts` - passed, 91 tests.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` - passed.
- `pnpm run eslint src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chat.shared.contribution.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/promptSyntax/promptFileRewriter.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/promptSyntax/promptToolsCodeLensProvider.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/promptSyntax/promptToolsCodeLensProvider.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` - passed.
- Commit hygiene hook - passed for all four files.

Live Code OSS testing with dbgjs verified explicit Copilot/VS Code targets, active-session fallback, namespace filtering, collapse/expand, bulk selection, qualified-name write-back, keyboard toggling, and Escape cancellation before the final child-label shortening. The shortened labels and retained full references are covered by the regression suite. Full integration and smoke suites were not run.

## Manual Testing

1. Open an `.agent.md` file containing `target: github-copilot` and `tools: [read, vscode/usages]`. Click **Configure Tools...**.
2. Expand **vscode**; verify children show names such as `usages` and `runTask`, not the namespace again. Select a group or individual tools and accept; verify qualified names are written to the header.
3. Toggle a tool with Space and press Escape; verify the header is unchanged.
4. Remove `target` and select a Copilot session; verify the same target-aware picker appears.
5. Set `target: vscode`; verify the existing VS Code picker is retained even while Copilot is active. Prompt files should also retain that picker.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The event multiplicity and full-tree reconstruction are explicit in the shared QuickTree implementation, and this diff directly adds the per-event render. Catalogue size controls magnitude, but the quadratic mechanism and UI-thread reachability are deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and QuickTree model/DOM reconciliation for all tool nodes
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N unique available tools, QuickTree's global check-all emits O(N) checkbox events, and this handler calls render/setItemTree over the O(N)-node catalogue for every event, producing O(N²) synchronous tree processing.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: main-thread CPU spikes and picker jank or dropped frames during bulk selection
Findings.PreviousBehavior: GitHub Copilot targets had no Configure Tools tree. Existing VS Code targets continue to use showToolsPicker and do not execute this new full-tree refresh handler.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every checkbox event in the new Copilot tree now invokes render(), which replaces the full item tree even when QuickTree has already updated the changed item and descendants in place.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `render();` at line 265 is inside `picker.onDidChangeCheckboxState`. The shared QuickTree controller's `checkAll` loops all nodes and fires onDidChangeCheckboxState for each changed node, so one user bulk-toggle reaches this added line once per node.
Findings.Title: Coalesce bulk checkbox tree refreshes
Findings.Impact: Clicking the picker’s global check-all control can synchronously reconstruct a large Copilot tool tree dozens or hundreds of times, visibly freezing or stuttering the Configure Tools UI as installed/client/MCP tool count grows.
Findings.Evidence: QuickTree.setItemTree drives QuickInputTreeController.setTreeData, which recursively maps the complete hierarchy and calls ObjectTree.setChildren. QuickInputTreeController.checkAll emits a checkbox-state event for each updated root and descendant. The catalogue's effective N is the unique names grouped from every active client's tools plus MCP wildcard entries and built-ins, so larger extension/MCP tool inventories amplify the repeated full-tree reconstruction.
Findings.Recommendation: Do not call setItemTree for each checkbox event. Let QuickTree's in-place checkbox propagation handle ordinary changes, update only dependent wildcard/all-tools items, and coalesce any required filtered-tree refresh to one microtask after a bulk operation.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed await, the first-snapshot implementation, and all transitive callers are directly traced. The exact snapshot duration varies by host/connection, which limits severity, but the cold critical-path latency change is deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: agent-host protocol subscription and first-snapshot IPC wait
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On a cold session, each tool consumer waits for the first snapshot from every matching harness; warm reads are immediate, but an unresponsive session can leave the wait pending indefinitely.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: blocked completion, hover, picker, and diagnostic latency during cold or stalled agent-host startup
Findings.PreviousBehavior: provideAgentFileTools synchronously read the currently cached inventory. If no first snapshot had arrived, it returned undefined immediately, so resolveAgentFileTools remained fail-open and completion/hover/validation could finish with built-in tools while the existing subscription loaded in the background.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added await blocks provideAgentFileTools until the asynchronous session-state subscription receives its first protocol snapshot. Because this provider is shared by resolveAgentFileTools, the wait is added not only to the new picker but also to existing completion, hover, and validation paths.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line `await this._customAgentsService.whenCustomizationsReady(sessionResource, token);` at line 332 precedes the formerly immediate `getAgentFileToolInventory` read. Existing callers in promptHeaderAutocompletion.ts:243, promptHovers.ts:208, and promptValidator.ts:413 all transitively invoke this method; the validator supplies CancellationToken.None.
Findings.Title: Keep the first agent-host snapshot off shared tool lookups
Findings.Impact: Opening or editing a GitHub Copilot agent before its remote/ambient agent-host snapshot arrives delays tool suggestions and hovers; diagnostics and Configure Tools also remain pending. A slow or stalled connection can keep these operations waiting indefinitely instead of returning the built-in/fail-open catalogue.
Findings.Evidence: WorkbenchAgentHostCustomizationService.whenCustomizationsReady creates/uses a session-state subscription and awaits `_awaitFirstSnapshot`, which resolves only on subscription change/error or cancellation and has no timeout. The prompt completion and hover providers await resolveAgentFileTools on interactive requests, while PromptValidator's visible-editor ModelTracker invokes it after edits with CancellationToken.None. Thus cold or stalled agent-host IPC now directly gates these consumers even though the old cached read returned immediately.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep provideAgentFileTools as a nonblocking cached read and put the readiness wait only in the new Configure Tools picker, where the busy UI and cancellation policy explicitly require a complete inventory. Alternatively add an explicit wait mode with cancellation/timeout so completion, hover, and validation retain the previous fail-open path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or edit a GitHub Copilot-targeted agent file and request tool completion, hover details, or diagnostics before the agent-host session snapshot is ready
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Completion and hover await resolveAgentFileTools before producing UI results; visible-editor validation awaits the same resolver before publishing markers. The changed provideAgentFileTools now requires the first session-state snapshot before any of these consumers can progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to agent-host session state and await the first snapshot
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced first-snapshot wait per session subscription, reached concurrently once per matching harness by each active tool-resolution caller
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: getAgentFileToolInventory ensured/read the in-memory subscription but returned undefined immediately when no snapshot existed, so interactive consumers did not await IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Introduced onto completion, hover, validation, and picker critical paths; these consumers cannot return until snapshot, error, or caller cancellation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One inventory lookup per matching harness per consumer invocation. Matching harnesses are resolved once and queried concurrently; catalogue processing then scales with the effective unique tool-name count after grouping. Repeated edits can start overlapping validator tasks because ModelTracker uses Delayer rather than ThrottledDelayer.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: resolveAgentFileTools uses Promise.all across matching harness descriptors. The agent-host service memoizes one readiness promise per session subscription, so concurrent callers coalesce on the same first snapshot, but each caller remains pending; validator calls use CancellationToken.None while completion/hover requests carry editor cancellation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm sessions return immediately because the session subscription already has a value. Cold sessions share a memoized readiness promise. There is no timeout or negative-cache completion for a stalled snapshot; before the diff, the inventory read returned undefined immediately and callers used the built-in/fail-open catalogue while the subscription populated in the background.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added await, first-snapshot implementation, and transitive callers were directly inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Snapshot latency depends on local versus remote agent host and connection health; warm sessions avoid the regression. The critical-path wait and lack of timeout for CancellationToken.None are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable latency regression because a shared provider change moves cold/stalled agent-host IPC onto several existing interactive and validation paths; readiness should be scoped to the new picker or explicitly bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke Configure Tools for a GitHub Copilot agent, load the catalogue, filter it, and toggle individual, group, namespace, All Tools, or global check-all selections
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The picker shows immediately in busy state, awaits all matching inventories, builds a unique-name/group tree, then synchronously filters or processes checkbox events on the UI thread. Accept rewrites the in-memory text model only after the picker closes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the current agent-file tool inventory from matching agent-host harnesses
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per matching harness, concurrently; each inventory serves the whole picker rather than one call per tool
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Copilot Configure Tools picker existed; non-Copilot targets used the existing VS Code picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Picker remains busy/disabled until all inventories resolve; introduced for the new Copilot picker.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Rebuild and reconcile the complete QuickTree hierarchy via setItemTree/setTreeData
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per checkbox event; global check-all emits an event for each changed tree node, causing O(N) full O(N) rebuilds
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This Copilot tree and its per-checkbox full render handler did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously during input and can block rendering/responding to the toggle.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N effective unique available tool names after grouping duplicate inventories, plus namespace/MCP wildcards and built-ins. Filtering is O(N) per keystroke. A global check-all emits O(N) checkbox events and the changed handler performs an O(N) setItemTree for each, yielding O(N²) synchronous tree work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Inventory requests run concurrently across harness descriptors with Promise.all. Picker interaction is single-threaded on the UI thread. There is no coalescing of checkbox-triggered render calls; cancellation hides the picker and cancels outstanding inventory waits.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold inventory waits on the shared session readiness promise; warm inventory reads current session state. The picker builds fresh maps/tree items per invocation and does not cache them, which is appropriate for current availability, but bulk render work is not batched.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: QuickTree.checkAll event emission, provider handler, and recursive setTreeData implementation were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installed/client/MCP tool counts vary, but inventories naturally aggregate all active-client tools and MCP servers. Exact frame loss depends on N and hardware; the quadratic event/rebuild relationship is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable synchronous UI regression for bulk selection because full-tree reconstruction is repeated per node instead of coalesced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke Configure Tools for a VS Code/default target, display code lenses, or rewrite selected tool names in prompt frontmatter
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Code-lens provision reads the cached parsed prompt model and returns one lens. VS Code/default targets invoke the existing showToolsPicker. On acceptance, formatting and one text-model edit complete the rewrite.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Formatting and parsing scale with the small frontmatter/tool-name list; code-lens work is once per provider request. Quote parsing remains linear in scalar length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new parallel work. The picker is one interactive operation; model version checks prevent concurrent stale rewrites.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: IPromptsService caches parsed prompt files by model version. Rewrites invalidate via model version naturally; no new long-lived cache or retained collection was added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High after tracing parser cache, code-lens provider, and rewriter.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; changed work is bounded by the current header and selected tools.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: target resolution, quote escaping, indentation preservation, and local model rewriting add bounded CPU/allocation and no expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench/editor feature registration and tool namespace augmentation during tool catalogue resolution
Scenarios.CriticalPath: PromptToolsCodeLensProvider is registered as an editor feature during the same shared contribution load where the module was previously side-effect imported. Namespace augmentation occurs after inventories resolve.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Registration is constant. Namespace augmentation checks two known namespace entries against the catalogue, O(2N), after effective inventory grouping.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new concurrency; catalogue inventory concurrency is covered in the picker/completion scenarios.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache lifecycle change. Known namespaces are static and added to each fresh catalogue only when absent.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from changed registration and static namespace definitions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; namespace count is exactly two.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: registration timing is equivalent and namespace scanning is tightly bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and all diff pages. Reported two introduced regressions: shared cold agent-host readiness now blocks existing tool consumers, and bulk checkbox handling performs quadratic synchronous tree rebuilds. Parser/rewriter, registration, static namespace augmentation, and VS Code picker paths are bounded and add no reportable boundary or lifecycle regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
